messages:
maria: odd one: our kotlin sample app doing streaming uploads on an older emulator (Android 11, API 30) shows duplicated POSTs when callTimeout kicks in during write. Noticing two POSTs where second has refreshed token. snippet below. anyone seen callTimeout+write interplay cause retries?

maria: scenario: large gzip stream, callTimeout=10s, writeTimeout default. If write hangs and callTimeout fires, OkHttp cancels call which sometimes leads to a recover/retry path while Authenticator also issues a follow-up after 401. server logs: 
[svc] 2026-03-10T11:00:01Z POST /upload 408 - "Auth: Bearer old"
[svc] 2026-03-10T11:00:01Z POST /upload 200 - "Auth: Bearer refreshed"

kai: callTimeout cancels whole call which may interrupt the write and close the socket -> triggers connection failure handling. If Authenticator also runs (401 path) you can get multiple attempts. callTimeout is global per-call; writeTimeout is per-write. If they overlap badly you can hit weird races.

omar: workaround ideas: 1) increase callTimeout for streaming endpoints, 2) make token refresh single-flight (mutex) so follow-ups don't multiply, 3) ensure retryOnConnectionFailure=false for heavy streaming clients.

maria: will try bumping callTimeout and disabling retryOnConnectionFailure for upload client. Also adding mutex around refresh in AuthenticatorBridge (runBlocking -> minimize blocking).

infra-bot: CI: UploadTimeoutRaceTest flaked on emulator-api30 in reproducible-upload branch. See job 4521 logs.

maria: PR planned: (a) client config example for streaming (long callTimeout, no retryOnConnectionFailure), (b) doc note about callTimeout vs writeTimeout interactions, (c) mutex-based refresh snippet. tagging @kai @omar for review. :thumbsup:
